title: Complementary, Not Cumulative: Interaction Effects in Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Navier-Stokes Vortex Shedding
abstract: arXiv:2608.19632v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) embed governing partial differential equations directly into the training loss, offering a promising alternative to costly CFD solvers for unsteady flows. Yet the growing list of techniques proposed to improve PINN training is typically validated one at a time, leaving open whether these techniques actually compose. We study this question in depth on the DFG/Schafer-Turek unsteady cylinder wake benchmark. In isolation, nearly every technique performs no better than an untreated baseline. However, combining periodic (SIREN) activations with causal weighting unlocks a previously inaccessible regime, reconstructing velocity and pressure fields to within 4.1% average relative L2 error against an OpenFOAM reference solution. translated_title: 互补而非累积：物理信息神经网络中Navier-Stokes涡脱落的交互效应
translated_abstract: 物理信息神经网络（PINNs）将控制偏微分方程直接嵌入训练损失中，为非定常流动提供了一种替代昂贵CFD求解器的有前景方案。然而，为改进PINN训练而提出的技术列表日益增长，通常每次只验证一种技术，这留下了这些技术是否能真正组合使用的疑问。我们在DFG/Schafer-Turek非定常圆柱尾流基准上深入研究了这个问题。单独使用时，几乎所有技术的表现都不优于未处理的基线。然而，将周期性（SIREN）激活函数与因果加权相结合，解锁了一个此前无法达到的机制，能够将速度和压力场重建到相对于OpenFOAM参考解的平均相对L2误差在4.1%以内。进一步添加其他技术反而导致灾难性的性能下降，这表明单独有效的PINN干预措施可能以非线性方式相互作用，并且更多并不总是更好。
tldr: 该论文发现，在物理信息神经网络中，技术改进并非简单累加，只有特定组合（SIREN激活与因果加权）能显著提升性能，而叠加其他技术会导致性能急剧恶化，揭示了干预措施间的非线性交互效应。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that improvements in physics-informed neural networks are not simply cumulative; only the specific combination of SIREN activations and causal weighting significantly enhances performance, while adding further techniques causes catastrophic degradation, demonstrating nonlinear interactions among interventions.
